children: A number of stocks fell in the afternoon session after recovering oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz and a projected fourth-quarter global crude surplus pushed Brent crude below $93 per barrel.

Brent futures fell below $93 a barrel and West Texas Intermediate slipped to roughly $87, CNBC data revealed. The International Energy Agency reversed its earlier deficit call, projecting fourth-quarter supply will average 105 million barrels per day, 1.7 million bpd above demand, while detailing 71 million barrels in emergency reserve releases, including 15 million barrels of diesel, by late February.

Wall Street is already marking down longer-term crude assumptions: Goldman Sachs projected in a client note cited by CNBC that Brent will average $88 in 2027 and ease to $78 by year-end as oversupply builds. Still, BMI analysts cautioned in research carried by CNBC that OPEC+ export recovery remains fragile after unverified Iranian reports of tanker mine explosions in the Strait of Hormuz.
The stock market overreacts to news, and big price drops can present good opportunities to buy high-quality stocks.
Among others, the following stocks were impacted:

children: Downstream refining & marketing company CVR Energy fell 6.1%.
Downstream refining & marketing company PBF Energy fell 4.3%.
Diversified upstream E&P company Petrobras fell 5.6%.

CVR Energy’s shares are extremely volatile and have had 39 moves greater than 5% over the last year. In that context, today’s move indicates the market considers this news meaningful but not something that would fundamentally change its perception of the business.
The previous big move we wrote about was 7 days ago when the stock gained 4.1% on the news that crude oil prices fell as President Trump played down the chance of new strikes on Iran.

CNBC reported that Brent crude dropped 0.75% to $97.57 a barrel, and West Texas Intermediate slipped 0.4% to $90.45. Trump said he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran if talks to end the conflict kept progressing. Attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz kept supply concerns in focus. CNBC also cited UBS, which said oil flows out of the Middle East are still elevated and are weighing on the physical market. A lower crude price can mean less cash from each barrel for oil and gas producers. That is a headwind for the energy group. Cheaper fuel can help heavy users of fuel, so the same move does not land the same way on every name in the group.

CVR Energy is up 52.9% since the beginning of the year, but at $38.53 per share, it is still trading 39% below its 52-week high of $63.12 from October 2026. Investors who bought $1,000 worth of CVR Energy’s shares 5 years ago would now be looking at an investment worth $2,055.
